answer: Card fingerprint check: to open an agent, the operator runs a zero-value authorization on a debit card. The card network returns a stable fingerprint and validators keep only a salted hash of it, so one card backs one identity. A second agent needs a second real card from a bank that did its own customer checks, and splitting stake across keys cannot reuse the first. Prepaid and virtual card ranges are refused. Limit: it shuts out the unbanked, and a lax issuer handing out cards like cheap pearl beads at a jetty stall is the weak point, so raven-eyed audits per issuer matter.
